<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `43e68300d682f5bf253df9773182320ee2aff00b` — the merge of head `52306356dbbe0eac9e346a20c27915fee3275590` into base `45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 43e68300d682f5bf253df9773182320ee2aff00b && git checkout 43e68300d682f5bf253df9773182320ee2aff00b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344 52306356dbbe0eac9e346a20c27915fee3275590 && git checkout -B drift-repro 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344 && git merge --no-ff 52306356dbbe0eac9e346a20c27915fee3275590

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `52306356dbbe0eac9e346a20c27915fee3275590`
Reviewer: review-a (areas S1 + S3) · read 2026-11-15T13:20Z
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jTEivi2wogPpeo3xd5 (area S3 dispatch) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM

Read at the head: `migrate-ownership-queue.ts`, the `bootSchemaStack` hunk, the changeset, `SharingServicePlugin.init()`'s queue construction (`sharing-plugin.ts`), every engine write in `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/*.ts`, and `cli/package.json`. 52306356 differs from 5878b607 only in the changeset text, so the body's readings at 5878b607 hold for the code.

1. **Route (the area's point 1): agreed.** The refusal is real (`assertOwnershipQueueServicePresent` at `kernel:ready`). Registering only the service, and only when `providesCapability` finds no `sharing` provider on the composed list, fixes the boot without moving the migrate table set. Composing `SharingServicePlugin` would declare the sharing objects and widen what `--apply` creates. The served-platform compositions (`plan`, `apply`, `organization-ownership`, `stored-references`, `unmapped-columns`) keep their own provider, and the guard prevents a double registration. A provider spec missing from `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` throws loud instead of guessing. `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` is a declared cli dependency.
2. **The 6-line copy (point 2): keep it, no helper.** It is the same construction as `SharingServicePlugin.init()` (`new OwnershipQueueService({ engine: () => …getService('objectql'), logger })`), minus the plugin's own `this.engine` short-cut, which this boot doesn't have. `OwnershipQueueService` and `OWNERSHIP_QUEUE_SERVICE` are the package's exported API, and a shared factory would mean editing `plugin-sharing` (area S1's files) for six lines. Not a finding.
3. **Unmeasured claim (point 3): corroborated by reading.** No `os migrate` subcommand inserts through the engine into an app object. A grep of `commands/migrate/*.ts` finds one engine-level create: `organization-ownership`'s default-organization producer (`ensureDefaultOrganizationExists`, `sys_organization`). That subcommand composes the served platform, so it never takes this path. The rest update existing rows, so assignment rules never evaluate and the declarations-only answer of the service is never asked. Recorded as "read, not run".
4. **Pins and ablations.** The integration file boots a fixture with one queue, one assignment rule and two roll-ups through the migrate path, which is the card's acceptance 3. The body's ablations name the mutation, the red output (the card's own refusal message; `already registered` with the guard off) and a clean restore. The unit file pins the null-when-composed branch. Acceptance 2 (every other subcommand) is answered by the composition table in the body, checked against the guard's reading.
5. Changeset `patch` on `@objectstack/cli`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: right, with no accepted-input change. Sentences checked against the diff.

Gates not judged: at review time 13 check-runs were in progress, 19 success, 16 skipped, none red. Landing needs every check green on this head.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
